newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares down at noon on A share weakness.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares down at noon on A share weakness.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index edged lower at midday on Friday, dragged down by weakness in the domestic A share market, analysts said.
The index lost 0.21 point or 0.16 percent to 129.39 on turnover of HK$19.5 million. The domestic A share index fell 1.10 points or 0.27 percent to 406.39 on turnover of 1.5 billion yuan.
"B shares were affected by the A shares," an analyst at J&A Securities (HK) said.
Brokers said A shares were hit by disappointment that no cut in bank reserve requirements was announced by the central bank on Friday. Market talk had suggested a cut as early as this week.
Brokers said there had been light buying earlier in the week on a possible move by the People's Bank of China to reduce the reserve requirement.

Shenzhen Special Econmic Zone Real Estate & Properties (Group) Co was the biggest B share loser, falling HK$0.17 or 6.34 percent to HK$2.51 on volume of 23,300 shares. Brokers have said they expected the company to report poor results for the first half of this year.
Bengang Steel Plates rebounded from its recent losses, rising HK$0.07 to HK$2.08 on the morning's heaviest volume of 1.2 million shares.
"Some big investors are trying to lift Bengang to make forthcoming new issues easier," an analyst at Guotai Securities said.
Bengang was the first B share listed so far this year to remain below its offer price of HK$2.38 per share.
But there were signs that some foreign investors were moving funds back into B shares from the Hong Kong stock market, where profit-taknng had emerged after a recent surge, analysts said.
Trading in Gintian Industry (Group) Co's A and B shares was suspended on Friday morning after the Shenzhen-based conglomerate announced its 1997 interim results.
The company posted net profits of 13.85 million yuan for the first half of the year, down 54 percent from 29.84 milion yuan in the year-ago period.
Gintian was the first of the 49 Shenzhen-listed B share companies to release its interim results.
Trading in its shares would resume in the afternoon. On Thursday, the firm's B shares closed at HK$2.41 each, while its A shares ended at 8.05 yuan.
